newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end sharply lower for third day.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end sharply lower for third day.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended sharply lower for the third day in a row Monday, with spot gold falling to a new 20 month low.

"We may be about to see a climactic sell off in gold as investment is sucked away into what could be a once-in-a-lifetime blow off rally in the stockmarket," said John Brimelow, New York director of international equities for South African bank BV Capital.
COMEX December gold ended down $1.80 an ounce at $374.50, after posting contract lows at $373.40. Back month in COMEX gold futures all saw life-of-contract lows also.

Spot gold in the bullion market ended quoted $374.350/85, after seeing new 20-month intraday lows around $373.00, following the London Monday afternoon fix at $375.40, and the New York close Friday at $376.10/376.60.
COMEX December silver closed down 11.5 cents at $4.720, a two week intraday low, though back months saw contract lows.

"Extraordinary upward momentum in equity markets, more sustained gains for bond prices, a softer-than-anticipated seasonal upturn in physical demand and prospects for producer forward selling are keeping gold prices on the defensive," Smith Barney analyst David Rinehimer said.

Commodity funds are holding record net short positions in COMEX gold futures, with large traders (non-commercials) net short net short 40,059 contracts in the latest CFTC Commitment of Traders data for the week ended November 19, published Friday night.

Implied lease rates in the bullion market have also climbed steadily in the past two months, with the one month rates jumping to 2.68 percent Monday, suggesting ongoing short selling by speculators, analysts said.
Meanwhile, hedging by gold miners in South Africa and Australia has been reported in recent days, as the price of gold has fallen sharply in Australian dollars and in South African rand.
Concern about European central bank gold sales was revived late last week also by reports the Swiss may be going to change their constitution to allow for a reduction in gold reserves.
Option volatilities have edged up as the key $374 and $370 support areas are being threatened in spot gold, but option volatility is still not far from historic lows.

Implied volatility for February gold is currently running around 5.75 percent for near-the-money options, below the 10.6 percent median of the past three years, Smith Barney options analyst Carmen Knoepffler noted.

However, the monthly OTC option expiry in London Wednesday and the U.S. Thanksgiving Holiday, which will close COMEX and NYMEX Thursday and Friday this week, may prompt some short covering later this week, traders said.
NYMEX January platinum ended down $4.80 an ounce at $382.00, also a contract low, while NYMEX December palladium was closed off $2.35 at $116.00, a contract low too.
-- Clive McKeef, New York Commodities 212-859-1641; email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
